accepted.question_text: Does every even integer greater than 2 admit a representation as the sum of two prime numbers? Equivalently, is Goldbach's conjecture true for all even integers larger than 2, or does there exist at least one even integer greater than 2 that cannot be written as a sum of two primes?
accepted.context_brief: Goldbach conjecture in additive number theory.

evidence.page: Main post blockquote, Goldbach conjecture statement
evidence.quote: Goldbach conjecture: Any even number larger than 2 is the sum of two prime numbers.

accepted.question_text: For the Collatz iteration defined by starting from a positive integer a0 and then setting an = 3a(n-1) + 1 when a(n-1) is odd and an = a(n-1) / 2 when a(n-1) is even, does every starting value eventually reach 1 after finitely many steps? Equivalently, is there any positive integer starting value whose Collatz trajectory never reaches 1?

evidence.page: Main post blockquote, Collatz conjecture statement
evidence.quote: Collatz conjecture: Choose some number a0. Define an by an=3an-1+1 if an-1 is odd or an-1/2 if an-1 is even. Then an will be 1 for some n.
